material_systems.name: Exterior Acrylic Latex Primer for Wood/Composite Trim

products: Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec EXT Primer
PPG Sun Proof Exterior Latex Primer
primer.notes: Standard exterior acrylic primer for wood and composite trim. Remains flexible long-term — resists cracking, peeling, blistering. For composite trim, also brush-seal all field-cut edges before full prime coat. Coverage rate is for smooth trim per Exterior_Primer_Systems_Doctrine.md §4 (400-450 SF/gal smooth). LF equivalent per PCA P10 one-foot rule: 1 SF = 1 LF for trim girth < 12 inches.

material_systems.notes: Primary primer for wood and composite trim on new construction. Composite trim field-cut edges must be sealed as separate task before full prime. Coverage assumes smooth mill finish — rough-sawn wood reduces coverage by 15-20%.

material_systems.name: Bonding Primer for PVC Trim

products: Benjamin Moore Insl-X Stix Bonding Primer
primer.notes: Mandatory for PVC (AZEK, Versatex) trim. Grips dense, non-porous surface while providing mechanical tooth for topcoat. Scuff-sand glossy surfaces with 220-grit before application. CAUTION: Bonding primer left exposed too long dries like 'peanut brittle' — loses flexibility for topcoat bond. Recoat within 1 week per Exterior_Primer_Systems_Doctrine.md §5.

material_systems.notes: PVC is non-porous — standard acrylic primer will NOT adhere. Bonding primer is non-negotiable for PVC trim. Higher coverage than acrylic on porous wood because PVC does not absorb primer.

material_systems.name: Alkyd/Shellac Spot Primer for Tannin Knots

products: KILZ Original Multi-Surface Stain Blocking Primer
primer.notes: Spot-applied to visible knots on tannin-rich species (cedar, redwood, Douglas fir) BEFORE full acrylic primer coat. Not a full-surface system — applied per knot/stain location. Alkyd has superior tannin stain blocking vs acrylic. Shellac-based (BIN) for extreme cases. Per Exterior_Primer_Systems_Doctrine.md §2: spot prime knots with alkyd before acrylic primer over remaining surface.

material_systems.notes: Conditional on wood species — only required for tannin-rich species (cedar, redwood, fir). Pine and spruce typically do not require knot spot-priming unless visible knots are present. Applied by brush to individual knots.

material_systems.name: Standard Exterior Acrylic Trim Paint

finish.notes: Standard production-grade 100% acrylic exterior trim paint. Good durability, color retention, mildew resistance. Smooth mill-finish trim provides consistent coverage. Two coats standard at QT3. Sheen is project-level selection (satin, semi-gloss, or gloss) — no locked-in default per RC-004.

material_systems.notes: Standard exterior trim system for QT3 new construction. Higher coverage than siding field due to smooth, sealed (primed) surface. NOT a fine-finish interior system — standard exterior grade per RC-007.

material_systems.name: Premium Exterior Acrylic-Urethane Trim Paint

finish.notes: Premium acrylic-urethane blend with enhanced hardness and scratch resistance. Superior color retention and fade resistance. QT4: light sand between coats on visible areas, raking light inspection. QT5: spray preferred for smoothest finish, hand-sand between coats. Sheen is project-level selection — no locked-in default.

material_systems.notes: Premium/superior exterior trim system for QT4 and QT5. Urethane additive provides harder film than standard acrylic — important for trim durability. Slightly lower coverage than standard due to higher solids content.

material_systems.name: Solar-Reflective Trim Paint for PVC

finish.type: IR-Reflective Acrylic with Complex Inorganic Color Pigments (CICPs)
products: Benjamin Moore Colors for Vinyl (select palette)
finish.notes: REQUIRED when substrate = PVC AND color LRV < 55. IR-reflective pigments allow dark visual colors while reflecting near-infrared radiation to reduce surface temperature. HARD STOP — standard dark paint on PVC causes excessive heat absorption, warping, buckling, and voids manufacturer warranty. Per Exterior_Color_Sheen_Configuration_Doctrine.md §1-2.

material_systems.notes: Conditional system activated by PVC substrate + dark color selection. Slightly lower coverage than standard acrylic due to specialty CICP pigment formulation. Sheen is project-level selection. Color palette is more limited than standard paint lines.

SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD.notes: New wood trim — smooth mill finish. Moderate absorption. Equivalent to ~425 LF/gal per PCA P10.

coverage_profiles.waste_notes: 15% material waste standard for trim per Exterior_Trim_Systems_Doctrine.md §7.

Wider fascia (10-12 inches) effectively doubles girth — may need SF-based calculation for boards >12 inches.
Spray application: multiply material quantity by 1.25-1.33 for transfer efficiency loss.

coverage_profiles.pca_p10_note: PVC trim with girth < 12 inches: 1 SF = 1 LF per PCA P10.

SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD.notes: PVC surface is non-porous — higher coverage than wood. Good primer build. 'SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD' state label used because PVC in NC context is bare/uncoated.

assumptions: PVC trim is consistently smooth and non-porous — predictable coverage.
No surface condition modifier needed — PVC does not have texture variation like wood.

coverage_profiles.pca_p10_note: All trim with girth < 12 inches: 1 SF = 1 LF per PCA P10.

SYS_EXT_TRIM_FINISH_SOLAR.notes: Solar-reflective formulation with CICP pigments — reduced coverage compared to standard.

coverage_profiles.waste_notes: 15% material waste standard for trim per Exterior_Trim_Systems_Doctrine.md §7.
assumptions: Coverage is per NET trim LF from PaintScope keys.
Two-coat system standard at all quality tiers.
Spray application: multiply material quantity by 1.25-1.33 for transfer efficiency loss.

consumables.name: Exterior Flexible Trim Caulk
consumables.usage_rate: 1 TUBE per 72 LF of joints (NC standard)
consumables.notes: Polyurethane or siliconized acrylic for trim joints. Per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine.md: NC caulk rate is ~72 LF per tube. Seal corner joints, trim-to-siding gaps, door/window casing joints. NEVER caulk window weep holes, bottom overlap of siding, or metal-to-wood flashing transitions. PVC substrate: use solvent-based polymer (NPC Solar Seal #900, OSI Quad) or polyurethane — NEVER silicone per Exterior_Trim_Systems_Doctrine.md §6. Polyurethane requires 3-7 day cure before painting per Exterior_Caulking_Sealants_Doctrine.md §1.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 80-120 Grit for Wood Mill Glaze
consumables.notes: Remove mill glaze from new wood trim. 80-120 grit range per Exterior_Trim_Systems_Doctrine.md §2. Hand blocks or orbital sander for field, blocks for edges and detail.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220 Grit
consumables.notes: Scuff-sand PVC trim (220-grit) before bonding primer. Also used for intercoat sanding at QT4/QT5 between finish coats. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 150 Grit
consumables.notes: General prep sanding and intercoat scuff sanding at QT4. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Tack Cloth
consumables.notes: Dust removal after sanding before prime or finish coat. Required after all sanding operations. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Acetone/Denatured Alcohol for PVC Prep
consumables.notes: Wipe cut edges of PVC trim with acetone or denatured alcohol to seal open cells and remove static charge per Exterior_Trim_Systems_Doctrine.md §2. Required before bonding primer on PVC.

consumables.name: Angled Sash Brush 2.5 inch
consumables.notes: Primary brush for exterior trim detail — casings, corners, sills, cut-in at glass and siding edges. Per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine.md: 1 brush per material type. ~5,000 LF lifespan with care. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Flat Brush 3 inch
consumables.notes: Secondary brush for wide flat trim runs — fascia, frieze, band boards. Faster coverage on flat profiles than angular sash brush. 1 per material type.

consumables.name: Airless Spray Tip 211 (trim detail)
consumables.notes: 211 tip code for narrow trim boards (casings, corner boards 3-4 inch width). Tight fan pattern for precision. Only applicable when application_method = spray.

consumables.name: Airless Spray Tip 313 (wider trim)
consumables.notes: 313 tip code for wider fascia, frieze, and band boards (6-12 inch width). Wider fan pattern for production. Only applicable when application_method = spray.

consumables.name: 60-Mesh Spray Filter (black) for Latex
consumables.notes: Standard 60-mesh (black) filter for latex exterior coatings through airless equipment. Change when flow rate drops. Only applicable when application_method = spray.

consumables.name: Painter's Tape (exterior grade)
consumables.notes: UV-resistant exterior masking tape. 14-day removal rating minimum for multi-day exterior projects. Used for glass masking at window/door casings, light fixture protection, and general edge masking. Per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine.md: all tape rolls yield 180 LF (60 yards). Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Masking Paper/Film for Glass Protection
consumables.notes: Masking film or paper for window/door glass protection when painting adjacent casings. Standard 180 LF rolls. Used in combination with masking tape for glass edge seal. Per research: this spec owns casing-to-glass edge masking (RC-002).

consumables.name: Plastic Sheeting / Landscape Tarps
consumables.notes: 4 mil minimum for landscape and hardscape protection. UV-resistant for multi-day exterior projects. Also used for siding masking when application_method = spray.

consumables.name: Canvas Drop Cloths
consumables.notes: Heavy canvas drop cloths for hardscape walkway protection below trim work area. Non-slip surface for crew traffic. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Caulk Gun
consumables.notes: Standard caulk gun for tube application. Included as consumable per crew — reusable across projects.

ext_landscape_adjacent.description: Landscape area adjacent to building below trim work zones
ext_landscape_adjacent.notes: Drop cloths/tarps along building perimeter where landscape beds, shrubs, and plants are adjacent. Brush: drop cloth at base. Spray: full tarp width over plantings.

ext_hardscape_walk.description: Adjacent walkways below trim work area
ext_hardscape_walk.notes: Canvas drop cloths for non-slip crew traffic. Plastic sheeting for spray overspray. Protection level driven by proximity and application method.

ext_window_glass_adjacent.description: Window glass adjacent to window casing trim being painted
ext_window_glass_adjacent.notes: Masking tape + film on glass to protect from brush drips and spray overspray during casing painting. This spec owns the casing-to-glass edge masking per RC-002.

ext_door_glass_adjacent.description: Door glass adjacent to door casing trim being painted
ext_door_glass_adjacent.notes: Glass masking when painting door casings. Same materials as window glass protection.

ext_light_fixture.description: Exterior light fixtures mounted on or near trim
ext_light_fixture.notes: Bag or tape over fixture. Remove fixture cover plate if accessible. Light fixtures commonly mounted on fascia or near trim.

ext_siding_adjacent.description: Siding adjacent to trim — masking required for spray application
ext_siding_adjacent.notes: When spraying trim, siding adjacent to trim must be masked to prevent overspray on finished or unfinished siding. Only applicable when application_method = spray. Brush application has minimal overspray — no siding masking needed. No dedicated PaintScope key — siding masking quantity is derived from trim LF being sprayed.

compatibility_rules.description: Bonding primer required for PVC trim
compatibility_rules.notes: Standard acrylic primer does NOT adhere to dense non-porous PVC surface. Bonding primer is mandatory.

compatibility_rules.description: Solar-reflective finish required for PVC with dark colors
compatibility_rules.notes: HARD STOP — standard dark paint on PVC causes thermal distortion (warping, buckling) and voids manufacturer warranty. Solar-reflective (VinylSafe) coating is non-negotiable when PVC + LRV < 55.

compatibility_rules.description: Knot spot-prime required for tannin-rich wood species
compatibility_rules.notes: Alkyd/shellac spot primer on visible knots before full acrylic primer coat. Prevents tannin bleed staining through finish.

compatibility_rules.description: Never use silicone sealant on PVC or any painted joint
compatibility_rules.notes: Silicone is not paintable and lacks bond compatibility with PVC. Use polyurethane, siliconized acrylic, or solvent-based polymer (NPC Solar Seal #900, OSI Quad) per Exterior_Trim_Systems_Doctrine.md §6 and Exterior_Caulking_Sealants_Doctrine.md §1.

compatibility_rules.description: Composite trim field-cut edges must be sealed
compatibility_rules.notes: All field-cut edges on engineered wood composite (LP SmartSide) must be sealed with primer + 100% acrylic latex paint before installation. Non-negotiable warranty requirement. Unsealed cut edges absorb moisture → edge swelling → paint film failure.

compatibility_rules.description: No primer needed when substrate is field-primed
compatibility_rules.notes: Skip prime module entirely when trim has already been field-primed in a prior mobilization. Direct topcoat application.

compatibility_rules.description: Caulk AFTER primer coat — never before
compatibility_rules.notes: Caulk adheres better to primed surfaces. Sequence: prep → prime → caulk → finish. Per research RC-003 and Exterior_Caulking_Sealants_Doctrine.md §3.

risk_notes.topic: PVC thermal distortion from dark paint
risk_notes.risk: Standard dark paint (LRV < 55) on PVC trim causes excessive heat absorption, leading to warping, buckling, and voided warranty.
risk_notes.mitigation: Use solar-reflective (VinylSafe) coating on ALL PVC trim with color LRV < 55. HARD STOP — no exceptions.

risk_notes.topic: Composite edge swelling from unsealed cuts
risk_notes.risk: Failure to seal field-cut edges on engineered wood composite allows moisture absorption into exposed wood fiber, causing edge swelling that ruptures paint film.
risk_notes.mitigation: Seal ALL field-cut edges with primer + 100% acrylic latex before installation. Warranty requirement.

risk_notes.risk: Cedar, redwood, and fir knots bleed tannins through standard acrylic primer, causing brown/yellow staining on finish coat.
risk_notes.mitigation: Spot-prime visible knots with alkyd or shellac-based primer (SYS_EXT_TRIM_PRIMER_ALKYD_SPOT) before full acrylic primer coat.

risk_notes.risk: Bonding primer left exposed too long (beyond 1 week) dries like 'peanut brittle' — loses flexibility needed for topcoat adhesion bond.
risk_notes.mitigation: Apply topcoat within 1 week of bonding primer application. If exceeded, scuff-sand before topcoat.

risk_notes.topic: Silicone sealant failure on PVC joints
risk_notes.risk: Silicone sealant lacks compatibility with PVC and is not paintable. Bond line failure allows water intrusion at caulked joints.
risk_notes.mitigation: Use solvent-based polymer (NPC Solar Seal #900, OSI Quad) or polyurethane sealant on PVC. Never silicone.

risk_notes.risk: Caulk beads are ~40 mils thick vs paint at 1-3 mils. Uncured caulk shrinks as it cures, cracking the paint film applied over it.
risk_notes.mitigation: Allow full cure per sealant type: acrylic latex can be painted after skinning; polyurethane requires 3-7 day cure.

risk_notes.topic: Adhesion failure from skipping PVC prep
risk_notes.risk: Painting over glossy PVC without scuff-sanding causes coating to peel in sheets. Bonding primer alone is insufficient without surface prep.
risk_notes.mitigation: Scuff-sand glossy PVC with 220-grit. Wipe cut edges with acetone/denatured alcohol. Then apply bonding primer.

material_quantity_notes.pca_p10_one_foot_rule: All trim with girth < 12 inches: quantify as 1 SF per LF. This conversion is already embedded in coverage profiles — LF/gal rates equal SF/gal rates for standard trim widths.
material_quantity_notes.waste_factor: 15% material waste standard for trim per Exterior_Trim_Systems_Doctrine.md §7. Applied to all primer and finish material quantities.
material_quantity_notes.spray_transfer_efficiency: Airless spray on trim: 50-70% transfer efficiency. Multiply theoretical coverage by 1.25-1.50 to account for overspray, misting, and pattern overlap. Tighter tip patterns (211) have better efficiency than wider (313).
material_quantity_notes.two_coat_standard: Standard coat system: 1 prime + 2 finish coats at all QTs on bare substrate. SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD skips prime coat (2 finish coats only).
material_quantity_notes.sill_extra_coat_note: Window sills may receive additional finish coat due to direct horizontal weather exposure — most vulnerable trim component.

assumptions.value: LF/gal rates equivalent to SF/gal per PCA P10 one-foot rule
assumptions.note: Doctrine confirms one-foot rule for trim girth < 12 inches. All 8 trim items in this spec fall within this range.
Doctrine confirms 400-450 SF/gal for smooth surfaces. Bonding primer slightly lower coverage due to higher film build.

assumptions.value: 72 LF per tube for new construction
assumptions.note: Doctrine confirms ~72 LF per tube for NC (more consistent gaps, higher volume).
No doctrine coverage for solar-reflective paint coverage rates. Derived from research and product data. Lower than standard acrylic due to CICP pigment formulation.
No doctrine-specific coverage for acrylic-urethane trim paint. Derived from research and PDS data. Higher solids = slightly lower coverage.

uncertainty_flags.description: Research suggests sills may need additional finish coat due to horizontal weather exposure. Not codified as standard — left as scope option.
uncertainty_flags.action: Flag for field calibration. May warrant separate sill coat count config.

uncertainty_flags.description: Acetone usage rate on PVC trim (1 QT per 200 LF) is estimated from research — no direct doctrine calibration.
